personally_read_before_design.requirement: Multiple players make simultaneous choices in active-player, then turn/seating order; the actions happen simultaneously afterwards. Do not use target-list order as player decision order.
An effect acting on multiple objects normally processes the action simultaneously. Sea God's Revenge's return is one batch, not sequential returns.

Ordinary competing replacements are selected by the affected object's controller (owner if there is no controller); repeat replacement checks for the modified event. Preserve that chooser identity and existing composition rather than treating all replacements as owner choices.

A commander moving to its owner's hand or library instead goes to command only if its owner chooses. Control changes do not transfer that choice. Graveyard/exile commander handling remains an SBA. A merged noncommander component keeps its appropriate destination.

additional_passages_personally_read.requirement: Library/hand/graveyard destinations belong to the owner, and a zone change creates a new object incarnation.
Retain pre-move characteristics and look-back information for the whole batch.
Keep ordinary replacement application lineage; the bounded repair does not rewrite repeated-replacement rules.
Scry 1 is a private top-card placement decision that occurs after the printed return instruction, not between returns.

oracle.name: Sea God's Revenge
oracle.oracle_text: Return up to three target creatures your opponents control to their owners' hands. Scry 1. (Look at the top card of your library. You may put that card on the bottom.)

complete_current_rulings_personally_read.comment: You can cast Sea God's Revenge with no targets. If you do, you'll scry 1 when it resolves. If you choose at least one target, and all chosen targets are illegal when Sea God's Revenge tries to resolve, it won't resolve and none of its effects will happen.
In multiplayer games, the three target creatures can be controlled by different opponents.

When you scry, you may put all the cards you look at back on top of your library, you may put all of those cards on the bottom of your library, or you may put some of those cards on top and the rest of them on the bottom.
You choose how to order cards returned to your library after scrying no matter where you put them.
You perform the actions stated on a card in sequence. For some spells and abilities, that means you'll scry last. For others, that means you'll scry and then perform other actions.

Scry appears on some spells and abilities with one or more targets. If all of the spell or ability's targets are illegal when it tries to resolve, it won't resolve and none of its effects will happen. You won't scry.

A call-local resumable zoneChangeReplacement in replacement.go advances deterministic ordinary replacements and pauses at controller decisions. No pending-choice state escapes into the Engine, catalog or Game.
